newsitem.title: USA: DC council to reconsider White House plan - paper.
newsitem.headline: DC council to reconsider White House plan - paper.

text.p: The District of Columbia Council has scheduled an emergency meeting on Friday to reconsider a proposed financial rescue plan from the White House, the Washington Post reported today.
The council had refused the plan earlier this week.

The Post reported that the Council's Acting Chairman Linda Cropp said she scheduled the meeting after White House officials agreed to add language to the proposal indicating that local and federal officials disagree over the proposed elimination of the $600 million federal payment to the city.
With that wording in place, there will be enough support on the Council to approve the rescue measure, Cropp told the Post.
Cropp city council members wanted to officially register their disagreement over the $600 million issue with the White House, teh Post reported.

The White House has said its rescue package would save the city about $800 million over five years by transferring several costly programs to the federal government. In exchange, it wants to eliminate the federal payment.
District officials have said that the city cannot afford to lose such a large chunk of revenue.
